publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

referenceList.doiPolicy: Datasets need a DOI or persistent identifier, preferably in URL format; epub-ahead-of-print articles are cited with the DOI in place of volume and page numbers

provenance.claim: mode: parenthetical-numeric — citation numbers are placed within parentheses and italicized
collapseRanges: true — '(18, 19) (18–20) (18, 20–22)': commas for collation, en dashes for ranges
authorTruncation.etAlAllowed: false — 'Do not use ... et al. (in place of the complete list of authors' names)'
per-type maxReferences: Research Articles about 50, extended format up to 100, Reviews up to 150, Perspectives 15
widthPresetsMm: single 90 / double 183 — the 2025 Guide to Preparing Figures fit box: '1 column = 21p3 picas (9 cm)', '2 column = 43p4 picas (18.3 cm)'
conflicting official widths (recorded, not encoded): the instruction pages state 5.7/12.1/18.4 cm for 1/2/3 columns; the 2025 guide reflects the current layout
lineWeightPt.min: 0.28 — 2025 guide: 'At final print size, minimum line weight is 0.28 pt (~0.10 mm)'
conflicting official line-weight minimum (recorded, not encoded): the instruction pages state 0.5 pt at the final reduced size
fonts: sans-serif (preferably Arial or Helvetica), labels 6–9 pt, panel letters 10 pt bold uppercase
redGreenDiscouraged: 'Avoid using combinations of red and green'

wordLimit.scope: stand-alone (~1000 words when linked to a paper)

provenance.claim: titleLimitChars: 96 — 'Titles should be no more than 96 characters (including spaces)'
research-article: main text up to 3000 words, abstract 125 words or less, 3 to 5 display items, about 50 main-text references
doubleSpacing: false — 'Use single spacing throughout the text, tables, figure captions, and reference list'
availabilityStatements data+code: Acknowledgments must end with 'Data, code, and materials availability:'

notes: Citation numbers are italicized inside parentheses: (18, 19), (18–20), (18, 20–22) — commas for collation, en dashes for ranges.

References are numbered in order of citation through: (i) main text, (ii) text boxes, (iii) figure and table captions, (iv) reference notes and acknowledgments, (v) supplementary materials; one single combined list covers paper + SM; each reference appears once with a unique number.
Do not use op. cit., ibid., or et al. — the complete author list is required in every reference (initials first, family names in full, commas between authors, no 'and').

Article titles are included and end with a period (shown in HTML, not print); journal titles italic; volume numbers bold (publication year substitutes when no volume); full page range with en dash; article number when pagination is not continuous; year in parentheses; entry ends with a period.

Personal communications may not be cited; 'in press' citations are not allowed at publication; preprints (arXiv, bioRxiv) may be cited (bioRxiv adds '[Preprint]' and the DOI, preferably as URL); any dataset with a DOI must be cited in the reference list; no citations in the Abstract.

Official sources conflict on column widths: instruction pages say 5.7/12.1/18.4 cm for 1/2/3 columns; the 2025 Guide to Preparing Figures gives 1 column = 9 cm and 2 columns = 18.3 cm (encoded here as the current layout).
Line-weight minimum likewise conflicts: instruction pages say 0.5 pt at final reduced size; the 2025 figure guide says 0.28 pt (~0.10 mm) at final print size (encoded).
Figure labels 6–9 pt sans-serif per the 2025 guide; web instructions add: lettering ~7 pt after reduction and not smaller than 5 pt, plot symbols 6 pt minimum, at most 3 type sizes per figure.

Panel letters: 10 pt bold uppercase A, B, C in the upper-left corner of each part (inside the perimeter for images); avoid subpart labels — if unavoidable use lowercase letters, primes, or lowercase roman numerals; numbers only for time sequences.
Full-color artwork must be provided in RGB; the figure of record is the RGB online version; print color charges: $650 for the first color figure, $450 each additional.

Avoid red and green together; avoid similar hues to identify different parts; avoid grayscale, light lines, and screen shading; use white (bold) type over dark/colored areas; no minor tick marks or grid lines; solid symbols preferred; SI units in parentheses; leading zeros on decimals.

colorAsSoleDelimiter is null: the official pages state no general color-as-sole-delimiter rule — the guidance is specific to red/green pairs (add strongly contrasting shades plus shapes or textures) and to colors similar in hue.
Figure captions: max 200 words each, single-spaced, begin with a short bold-face title; figure title belongs in the caption, not in the figure.

Research Articles carry 3 to 5 display items; extended format up to 6 (may include videos) and must be justified in the cover letter; meta-analyses needing more than 250 total references must contact the editors before submission; Reviews under 20% self-citation.

Initial submission: single .docx with figures/tables embedded (LaTeX users convert to .docx or use the Science LaTeX template and upload a PDF) plus a combined PDF; revised: one .docx WITHOUT embedded figures, each figure as a separate PDF/EPS/AI/TIFF file; PowerPoint not accepted.

Raster resolution: 300 dpi minimum at final size (photographic images 300–500 dpi per the 2025 guide); upsampling not permitted; do not rasterize, flatten, or outline text — keep labeling on editable layers.

Materials and Methods go in the supplementary materials and must allow replication; Acknowledgments must contain, in order: contributions, Funding, Author contributions (CRediT encouraged), Competing interests (declared even if none), and Data, code, and materials availability.

Single spacing throughout text, tables, captions, and references; US letter page; Times New Roman preferred for manuscript text; avoid Symbol fonts; ORCID iD required for first and corresponding authors at revision.

Titles: no more than 96 characters including spaces; no paragraph breaks in title, author list, or abstract; Research Article abstracts are unstructured with prescribed flow (background, objectives/methods, results, conclusions).

COVER-LETTER RULES — QUOTE PROVENANCE: the `letters` block below carries source URLs but NO verbatim quotes.
